fields.meta_title: Telehealth Landing Page Builder for Clinics | Emergent
fields.meta_description: A telehealth landing page books the video visit before anyone joins a call. See four practice examples and build one with visit reminders.
fields.h1: Build a Telehealth Landing Page That Books Virtual Visits
fields.hero_description: Build a telehealth landing page that books video visits and saves each request to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: Six Pieces Behind a Booked Video Visit
fields.features_subheading: The booking happens on the page, well before the video call. Describe the practice, and Emergent builds these parts.
fields.feature_1:
A state picker at the top of the form

The form asks where the patient will be when the call starts, and it lists only the states the practice serves. Anyone outside them gets a short note and an email field.
fields.feature_2:
Visit length and price beside the button

Name the visit the page books, its length, and the self-pay price in the prompt, and the page shows all three beside the button. A visitor reads the cost before booking.
fields.feature_3:
A 911 notice above the first field

Put one line above the form telling visitors to call 911 in an emergency, and saying requests are read during office hours. Visitors see that notice before any other field.
fields.feature_4:
Requests kept in a table you own

Every booking request lands as a row in a database you own, with the state, the visit time, and the time it arrived. Connect the rows to a scheduling tool over its API.
fields.feature_5:
A reminder email before each visit

The app emails each patient an hour before the video visit, with the link the practice uses and a way to pick a new time. Change the timing by prompt, such as 2 hours before.
fields.feature_6:
The page as code in your repository

Export the page and its request table to your GitHub repository on paid plans. Or keep it hosted on Emergent on the practice's own domain, which uses credits, and edit by prompt.

fields.tab_content_1:
7 visitors from outside the six states joined a list

Larkspan Virtual Care sees patients in six states, and its form asks which state each visitor will be in during the visit. A visitor who picks Another state sees a short note and leaves an email in place of a booking. This week 84 visitors filled in the form: 77 booked, and 7 picked Another state.
fields.tab_content_2:
With one button, 2 of Wednesday's 14 patients moved

An hour before each video follow-up, the Copperleigh Family Medicine app emails the patient the visit link and a Pick a new time button. On Wednesday 14 follow-ups were booked, and 14 reminders went out. Twelve patients kept their time, and 2 used the button to move to Thursday.
fields.tab_content_3:
For self-pay, a video visit is $65, stated first

Orrin Vale Skin Clinic puts its price above the form: a 15-minute video visit for a skin concern costs $65 self-pay. Each visitor then picks Self-pay or Insurance. This month 52 requests came in, 34 of them self-pay, and the 18 insurance requests were emailed to Corwin Ahlberg, the billing coordinator.
fields.tab_content_4:
Every Spanish request goes by email to Dr. Fairbairn

Hollins Reach Health asks one question up front: English or Spanish for the visit. A Spanish request is emailed to Dr. Renata Fairbairn, who sees patients in both languages, and English requests go to the front desk. This week 38 requests came in, with 15 asking for Spanish and 23 for English.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Telehealth Landing Page
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to a telehealth landing page that books video visits in the states you serve, then build it with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Choose the one visit the page books
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 List the states the practice serves
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Show the price beside the button
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Keep the form to contact and timing
fields.howto_step_1_des: Pick a single visit type, such as a 20-minute video follow-up or a first visit for a skin concern. A page that books one visit can state its length and price plainly, and its booking button has one job to do.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Ask each clinician which states they see patients in, and give Emergent that list for the state picker. Review it whenever a clinician joins or leaves. The form should never offer a state that nobody on staff covers.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Write the self-pay price as a number, such as $65, along with the visit length and whether the practice takes insurance. Place all of it beside the booking button, and change it by prompt on the day the price changes.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Ask for a name, an email or phone number, the state, and a preferred time. Leave symptoms and medical history for the intake the clinician uses after booking, and say so in one line under the form.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Spell out the time zone after booking
fields.howto_step_5_des: Show the visit date and time on the confirmation with the zone written out, such as 10:20 am Eastern. Add what the patient needs for the call: a phone or laptop with a camera, and a quiet room.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Publish on the practice's web address
fields.howto_step_6_des: Put the page on the practice's own domain (built into Emergent, uses credits). The link in every reminder email then carries the name patients already know. Custom domains are included in Emergent and use credits, and the free tier covers building and publishing.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Book a test visit from a phone
fields.howto_step_7_des: Book a visit on a phone the way a patient would, then wait for the reminder email and open it. Check that the visit link works, that Pick a new time updates the row, and that the booking shows the right state.

faq_plan.q: What is a telehealth landing page?
faq_plan.a: A telehealth landing page is a single web page that books one kind of virtual visit with a practice, such as a video follow-up. It shows the visit's length, its price, and the states served beside a short form, and keeps each request for the practice to act on.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a telehealth landing page?
faq_plan.a: Tell Emergent's AI landing page builder what the visit is, what it costs, where the patients are, and who answers each request. It builds the page and stores requests in a table, and a later prompt changes any part.

faq_plan.q: What should a telehealth landing page show above the fold?
faq_plan.a: Lead with the name of the visit, how long it runs, what it costs, which states are covered, and the booking button. Add a real photo of the clinician who runs the visits in place of stock art. Move bios and insurance details further down the page.

faq_plan.q: Should a clinic keep its telehealth landing page separate from its in-office booking page?
faq_plan.a: Yes, when the two visits differ in length, price, or where the patient can be. A clinic with a chiropractic landing page for adjustments in the office can run a second page for video follow-ups, with its own form and state picker. Emergent builds each page from its own prompt.

faq_plan.q: Which fields should the form on a telehealth landing page ask for?
faq_plan.a: Four: the patient's name, one way to reach them, the state they will be in during the call, and a preferred time. Questions about symptoms belong in the intake that follows booking. On a page Emergent builds, every answer lands in a database you own, one row per request.

faq_plan.q: How should the emergency notice on a telehealth landing page be worded?
faq_plan.a: Plainly, in one or two short sentences, such as "In an emergency, call 911. Requests sent here are read during office hours." Repeat the same lines on the confirmation screen, where a visitor lands right after booking.

faq_plan.q: Can a dental office use a telehealth landing page for video consults?
faq_plan.a: Yes. A video consult page books the call and states its price, while the office's dentist landing page keeps booking cleanings and other visits in the chair. Give each page a different button label. A visitor then knows which kind of visit they are booking.

faq_plan.q: How should a telehealth landing page handle time zones?
faq_plan.a: Show every open time in the visitor's own time zone, and write the zone out next to it, such as 3:40 pm Central. Ask for this in the prompt. Repeat the zone in the confirmation and in the reminder email. A patient in another zone then joins at the right hour.

faq_plan.q: What should a telehealth landing page send as a visit reminder?
faq_plan.a: An email with the date and time, the time zone, the visit link, a button for a new time, and a phone number to call if the link fails. Emergent builds the reminder from your prompt, and the app sends it on the schedule you set, such as a day before and an hour before.

faq_plan.q: Can therapists use a telehealth landing page for online sessions?
faq_plan.a: Yes, for booking them. Keep the form to contact details and timing, and state the session length and fee before the button. A practice that also wants therapist bios and free consultation calls can start from a mental health landing page instead.

plan.angle: Searchers for telehealth landing page find template galleries and design roundups that show a clean hero with a doctor on a laptop, never the booking logistics a virtual visit needs. This page shows four telehealth pages built around those logistics (a state picker that keeps requests inside the states a practice serves, a reminder email before each video visit, a self-pay price shown above the form with insurance requests routed to billing, a visit-language choice routed to a Spanish-speaking clinician), each with the form, the routing and the database row behind it, and gives the build steps: one visit type per page, the states served, the price and the length, a contact-only form, a notice to call 911 in an emergency, and a confirmation that states the time zone. It makes no treatment, licensure, insurance-law or privacy-law claims. Dentist, chiropractic and mental health pages are siblings and stay out of the headings.
